data.decision: Fix PJAN-24 with the ticket's inline guard, not by converging onto WireMiseOpInject's inject-op-secrets.sh
data.reasoning: Two viable fixes exist. (a) The ticket's own proposal: guard the rendered hook on .env.op existence plus op availability and terminate with || true. (b) Converge the copier template and parity audit onto src/commands/WireMiseOpInject.ts, which already implements a stronger pattern (TTL, mktemp plus atomic mv, account probe). Choosing (a). Option (b) relocates the materialized secrets destination from .env to .env.secrets, which changes the _.file contract for every already-provisioned repo and would silently stop populating .env for consumers that read it directly - a behavior change well beyond a data-loss bugfix, and one that cannot be rolled back per-repo once templates re-render. Option (a) is confined to the hook string and its matching audit assertion, satisfies the stated AC exactly, and leaves (b) available later as a deliberate migration. Non-negotiable constraint on the implementation: src/parity/index.ts:2656 currently requires the literal unguarded string, so the template change and the audit assertion must land in the same commit or audit will fail every repo that receives the fix.

data.decision: Surface a structural gap: the tp adapter cannot see ticket attachments at all, so attachment-based specs are invisible to both Momo and Hermes
data.reasoning: Momo's operating rules treat attachments as frequently the PRIMARY specification - richer and more current than the written description. But the sanctioned adapter contract (agents/hermes/pm/.scripts/lib/ticket-provider.sh:14-15) returns exactly eight keys - id, key, title, description, acceptance, state, state_type, comments - and Plane stores attachments behind a separate /issue-attachments/ endpoint the adapter never calls. Verified across all twelve open tickets: no attachments key is present on any payload, which is a property of the adapter rather than evidence that no attachments exist. The practical consequence is that neither Momo nor Hermes can satisfy the inspect-attachments-before-scoping rule on this board, and an un-inspected attachment cannot even be detected to block on. Corroborating signal: PJAN-15 and PJAN-16 are raw unpunctuated voice-note transcripts pasted into the description, strongly implying original audio attachments that the adapter cannot surface. Recording rather than silently proceeding, because the 2026-07-28 Trello #158 incident - an entire ticket mis-scoped because its attached video was never opened - is exactly this failure mode. Remedy belongs with PJAN-23, which already owns extending the tp adapter contract.

data.decision: HOLD PJAN-24: the ticket's prescribed inline guard is provably insufficient; require atomic temp-file write, superseding my earlier approach decision
data.reasoning: I previously chose the ticket's inline-guard approach over converging on WireMiseOpInject, reasoning that the latter relocates secrets to .env.secrets and changes the _.file contract. That reasoning was sound about the destination but wrong about sufficiency. Empirical test: with .env.op present and op installed but the op session expired, the guarded hook truncated a populated .env to 0 bytes and exited 0. Both guards PASS in that scenario so they never engage, and > truncates the redirect target before op inject executes; || true then hides the failure. The guards only cover missing-.env.op and missing-op, while expired-session is the most common real-world path. The ticket's own proposed fix therefore closes roughly two thirds of the hole and leaves the likeliest third open while appearing correct - a worse outcome than the original bug because it manufactures false confidence. Correct fix keeps the guards, keeps .env as the destination so no _.file contract changes, and adds the atomic pattern already proven in src/commands/WireMiseOpInject.ts:40-51 - write to a mktemp sibling, replace via mv only on op success, clean up the temp on failure. This is a repair of my own earlier call, recorded so the trail shows why the approach changed mid-ticket.

data.decision: Escalate PJAN-24: both guards are inert by construction in every pjangler-provisioned repo, so the committed fix closes zero live paths
data.reasoning: Independent spec review surfaced, and I verified directly, that the guard conditions can never fire in the target population. .env.op is tracked in pjangler's own repo (git ls-files confirms), the CommonProject template SHIPS template/.env.op so every provisioned repo receives one, and .gitignore:46 carries an explicit !.env.op negation with a comment stating it IS committed. Guard one (.env.op exists) is therefore always true by design; guard two (op on PATH) is true on any operator machine. For real 33GOD repos the only thing standing between a populated .env and truncation is op itself succeeding, and expired-session, not-signed-in, unreadable-item and offline are routine rather than exotic. The committed fix is thus cosmetic for the population it ships to, which is the same false-confidence failure that caused this ticket to be closed prematurely once already. Two further blocking defects came from the same review: the audit asserts presence of the guard rather than absence of the legacy form, so a repo carrying BOTH hooks passes with empty details while still truncating; and the new isOpInjectHookEntry fallback matching any hook containing op inject plus .env.op is a REGRESSION against main that silently rewrites a user's -o .env.secrets or > .env.local hook to target .env, introducing a data-loss vector the fix itself created. All three are in scope for this ticket rather than follow-ups, because closing PJAN-24 on the current branch would mark a data-loss bug done while the loss remains live.

data.decision: CommonProject template changes have not been reaching generated projects since 2026-06-04; fix by passing --vcs-ref=HEAD to the copier invocation
data.reasoning: PJAN-31a merged with every gate green - submodule contract verified against remote, gitlink published, 21 suites passing, template file present in the pinned commit - and still shipped nothing. A real copier render into a real directory produced .github/workflows as an EMPTY directory. Cause: src/project/index.ts builds the CommonProject copier command without --vcs-ref, so copier renders from the newest git tag (0.2.5, dated 2026-06-04) rather than HEAD. Reproduced both ways against the identical template and data: without the flag the workflow is absent, with --vcs-ref=HEAD it renders correctly. The blast radius is 23 commits of template work since that tag, which reach generated projects only where a parity rule coincidentally re-applies the same change - mise.toml appears current for exactly that reason, which initially masked the diagnosis and caused me to wrongly retract the tag hypothesis before re-confirming it. Fix follows the precedent already in the codebase at src/commands/hermes/RunCopierTemplate.ts:137, which passes --vcs-ref=HEAD for the hermes-agent template; only the CommonProject path was missed. Tradeoff accepted: HEAD means the template is whatever is committed, with no release gating, which matches the operator's stated preference for changes shipping immediately. This is the strongest evidence yet for the operator's no-fixtures rule - every indirect check passed and only a real render exposed it.
